record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM, where the input is n positive integers b_1, ..., b_n and the task is to decide whether there exist two disjoint non-empty subsets with the same sum, can one design exact algorithms faster than the known O*(2^n) approach obtained by translating the instance to Table-4-SUM, and can one clarify how fast algorithms for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM relate to fast algorithms for SUBSET-SUM?

evidence.quote: It might be interesting to design faster algorithms for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM, and to get some understanding of the relationship between fast algorithms for SUBSET-SUM and fast algorithms for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM is the following decision problem: given n positive integers b_1, ..., b_n, decide whether there exist two disjoint non-empty subsets A, B ⊆ {1, ..., n} such that Σ_{i∈A} b_i = Σ_{i∈B} b_i. A baseline exact algorithm runs in O*(2^n) time (where O* hides factors polynomial in n) via reduction to a 4-SUM-style tabulation. SUBSET-SUM is the related problem of, given positive integers b_1, ..., b_n and a target t, deciding whether some subset sums to t; it admits an O*(2^{n/2}) meet-in-the-middle algorithm.

(a) Design an exact algorithm for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM whose worst-case running time is strictly better than O*(2^n) (and ideally better than the meet-in-the-middle bound O*(3^{n/2}) ≈ O*(1.7321^n)).

(b) Clarify the relationship between the time complexities of exact algorithms for SUBSET-SUM and for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM: in particular, determine whether a faster-than-2^{n/2} algorithm for SUBSET-SUM yields a correspondingly faster algorithm for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM, and conversely.
artifact.status_search_result: Part (a) has been partially resolved: Mucha, Nederlof, Pawlewicz, and Węgrzycki (ESA 2019) gave a Monte Carlo algorithm running in O*(1.7088^n) time, beating the meet-in-the-middle bound of O*(3^{n/2}) and hence the trivial O*(2^n). They also obtained an O*(2.6817^n) polynomial-space algorithm. The precise relationship between the complexities of SUBSET-SUM and EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM (part b) does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Equal-Subset-Sum Faster Than the Meet-in-the-Middle
status_evidence.snippet: O*(1.7088^n) Monte Carlo algorithm improving on the O*(3^{n/2}) meet-in-the-middle, answering an open problem from Woeginger's survey.
status_evidence.claim: An algorithm faster than 2^n (and faster than meet-in-the-middle) for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM has been found.

status_evidence.title: Faster algorithms for k-subset sum and variations
status_evidence.snippet: Further improvements and generalizations to k-subset-sum variants building on the Mucha et al. result.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work continues to improve and generalize EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM algorithms.
